# 16s-amplicon-sequence-denoising

## Summary

Denoises Illumina-amplified 16S rRNA reads with the Deblur pipeline to infer bacterial amplicon sequence variants (ASVs) at the genus level, replacing OTU binning with a static error model suited to shorter fragments.

## When to use

Use when raw 16S amplicon FASTQ reads (e.g. paired-end Illumina MiSeq 2 x 300 bp from hypervariable-region libraries) must be denoised into genus-level ASVs prior to taxonomic assignment.

## When NOT to use

- Input is already a denoised ASV/OTU feature table rather than raw FASTQ reads
- Reads are long full-length 16S rRNA sequences from third-generation (e.g. Nanopore) platforms, since Deblur is recommended for shorter bp fragments

## Inputs

- Paired-end 16S amplicon FASTQ files (2 x 300 bp Illumina MiSeq reads from V1–V2, V3–V4, V5–V7 and V7–V9 library pools)
- Non-chimeric 16S rRNA reference database from QIIME 2

## Outputs

- Denoised bacterial ASV feature table (ASVs per sample)
- Representative ASV sequences ready for genus-level taxonomic assignment
- Chimera-filtered reads (best hit similarity >= 99%)

## How to apply

First assess per-base quality with FastQC (Version 0.11.9 in this study) and filter raw reads to Q30, trimming to a uniform length suitable for Deblur, which is recommended for shorter bp fragments. Run the Deblur pipeline on the quality-filtered paired-end reads to infer ASVs and delete non-redundant reads, using its static error model instead of OTU clustering. Screen the denoised reads against the non-chimeric 16S rRNA database from QIIME 2, removing reads whose best hit similarity rate is less than 99% to eliminate chimeras. Export the denoised ASV feature table and representative sequences so that taxonomy can be assigned against Greengenes and collapsed at the genus level. Note that in this study DADA2 identified more real variants than other methods, so denoiser choice is a documented decision point.

## Related tools

- **Deblur** (Denoising algorithm that infers bacterial ASVs at the genus level from quality-filtered 16S reads, deleting non-redundant reads using a static error model) — github.com/ruben-aladid/-Hypervariable-regions-of-16S-rRNA-with-the-highest-resolving-power-for-taxonomic-identification
- **FastQC** (Pre-denoising quality control: obtain Q30 quality sequences and inspect reads per sample, bases per sequence, and sequence length distribution)
- **QIIME 2** (Provides the non-chimeric 16S rRNA database used to identify chimeras, removing reads with best hit similarity below 99%)

## Examples

```
deblur workflow --seqs-fp filtered_reads/ --output-dir deblur_asvs --min-reads 10 --mean-error 0.005
```

## Evaluation signals

- Per-base quality profiles from FastQC confirm reads meet the Q30 cutoff before denoising
- Chimera screening against the QIIME 2 non-chimeric 16S rRNA database shows no retained read with best hit similarity < 99%
- Denoised output is a non-redundant ASV table (redundant reads deleted) rather than OTU clusters
- Representative ASV sequences successfully receive genus-level assignments against Greengenes and collapse to genus level
- Downstream alpha diversity (e.g. Kruskal–Wallis between hypervariable-region groups) and rarefaction curves behave as expected on the denoised table

## Limitations

- Denoiser choice matters: DADA2 identified more real variants and output sequences than other methods in this study's comparison
- Deblur is recommended for shorter bp fragments; the 300 bp length limit of the Illumina MiSeq platform limits 16S rRNA profiling
- Taxonomy depends on the reference database: regions were trained with Greengenes despite more updated SILVA versions being available
- Mock microbial communities contain only 10 species, which affects the sensitivity and specificity of taxonomic classification used to validate the pipeline

## Evidence

- [methods] Sequence denoising was performed with the Deblur pipeline, which is intended for paired-end data, and the non-redundant reads were deleted: "Sequence denoising was performed with the Deblur pipeline, which is intended for paired-end data, and the non-redundant reads were deleted"
- [methods] The non-chimeric 16S rRNA database from QIIME 2 was used to identify chimeras in the reads, with a best hit similarity rate of less than 99%: "The non-chimeric 16S rRNA database from QIIME 2 was used to identify chimeras in the reads, with a best hit similarity rate of less than 99%"
- [results] FastQC was used to obtain quality sequences with Q30 and to observe the number of reads per sample: "FastQC was used to obtain quality sequences with Q30 and to observe the number of reads per sample"
- [discussion] First, DADA2 identified more real variants and output sequences than other methods: "First, DADA2 identified more real variants and output sequences than other methods"
